about.title: Antioch Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Most of us in Antioch don't think twice about the things we rely on every day: the brakes on a car merging onto SR-4, a space heater in a Hillcrest Avenue apartment, a child's car seat, a power tool from a store on Lone Tree Way. When one of those products is defective and someone gets hurt, California law takes a different path than an ordinary negligence case. Under strict liability, you generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You need to show the product had a defect — in its design, in how that unit was made, or in the warnings that came with it — and that the defect caused your injury. Responsibility can reach the manufacturer, the distributor, and the Contra Costa County retailer that sold it. Antioch recorded 293 injury collisions in 2025, and some crashes trace back to a part that failed rather than a driver's mistake. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Antioch residents with an independent attorney who works on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Antioch Residents Use LawProactive for Product Claims

items.title: Strict Liability Changes the Question
items.desc: In California you generally don't have to prove the company was negligent — only that the product was defective and the defect caused your injury. An attorney who works these cases knows how to frame a design, manufacturing or warning defect from the start.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: The broken item, its packaging and any receipts are often the heart of the claim. The attorneys we connect you with can advise right away on keeping the product intact and untouched before evidence is lost.

items.title: More Than One Party May Owe You
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors and the Antioch or Contra Costa County retailer that sold the product may each share responsibility. Independent counsel can identify every party in the chain instead of stopping at the brand name on the box.

items.question: My brakes or tire failed on SR-4 near Antioch. Is that a car accident case or a product case?
items.answer: It can be both. If a defective part caused the crash, you may have a strict liability claim against the manufacturer alongside any claim involving another driver. Do not have the vehicle repaired or scrapped until an attorney has a chance to look at the failed component — that part is your key evidence.

items.question: Do I really need to keep the broken product?
items.answer: Yes, whenever it is safe to do so. Store the product, its packaging, manuals and receipt exactly as they are, and photograph everything, including where the failure happened. If the item is hazardous, like a swollen battery, keep it isolated rather than throwing it away, and tell your attorney so it can be handled properly.

items.question: Can I hold the store in Antioch that sold it responsible, or only the manufacturer?
items.answer: Under California's strict liability rules, retailers and distributors in the chain of sale can be liable along with the manufacturer. That matters when the maker is overseas or hard to reach. An attorney can sort out which parties to pursue, and the attorneys in our network charge no fee unless there is a recovery.
